strategy.bottleneck: [memory-bound, transaction-inefficient] gn_apply2 (134.0 µs, the largest non-conv kernel, ~53% of the 251 µs custom-kernel time) moves the minimum 3×67 MB yet reaches only 67.59% DRAM vs 82.26% for gn_apply1 on identical traffic: 4-byte scalar loads/stores plus a 34,816 B/block shared tile cap it at 6 blocks/SM (75% theoretical occupancy), so long-scoreboard stalls (71.66%) are never hidden.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: mem_vectorize the NHWC→NCHW epilogue: retile gn_apply2 to 64 pixels × 64 channels so both the NHWC read and the NCHW residual-add/store use 16-byte float4 accesses instead of scalar 4-byte ones. This quarters memory instructions and in-flight requests per byte (fixing the 71.66% long-scoreboard stall with only 0.54 eligible warps/scheduler), and shrinks shared memory from 34 KB to ~16.6 KB, lifting the shared-mem block limit from 6 to ≥12 so latency is hidden by concurrency.
strategy.modification_plan:
Target: gn_apply2 only. Keep both at::conv2d calls, gn_stats_p1/p2 and gn_apply1 untouched.

1. Replace the 4 scalar global ops per element in gn_apply2 with float4 ops: read y2 (NHWC) as `const float4*` (4 channels per thread), and write `out` / read `res` (NCHW) as `float4` over 4 contiguous pixels. Exact action: delete the `for (j<np) base[(p0+j)*NCH+c]` scalar loop and the `for (cc=warp;cc<NCH;cc+=8) out[off]=v+res[off]` scalar loop.
2. Retile: PT=64 pixels × CT=64 channels per pass; smem budget check = 64 rows × (64+1) floats × 4 B = 16,640 B per block (single buffer) << 227 KB per-block limit and ≤ 228 KB/SM at 8 blocks, so staging is legal; declare `__shared__ float sm[64][65]` (pad 1 avoids the 8-way conflict of an unpadded 64 stride). Grid = (ceil(npix/64), B), block = 256, and an inner loop over the 4 channel tiles c0 = 0,64,128,192.
3. Load phase (per channel tile): thread t → p = t>>4 (16 pixels/iter, 4 iters to cover 64), v = t&15. Address `((const float4*)(y + b*npix*256 + (p0+p)*256 + c0))[v]` — always 16 B aligned since 256 and c0 are multiples of 4. Apply `v*scale[c]+shift[c]` then silu per component with scale/shift preloaded into registers (channels c0+4v..+3), and store transposed: `sm[4v+k][p] = silu(...)`.
4. `__syncthreads();`
5. Store phase: thread t → ct = t>>4 (16 channels/iter, 4 iters), v = t&15. Build `float4 r = {sm[ct][4v], sm[ct][4v+1], sm[ct][4v+2], sm[ct][4v+3]}`, load `float4 rr = ((const float4*)(res + b*256*npix + (c0+ct)*npix + p0))[v]`, add, and store to the matching `out` float4. This makes each channel row a 256 B contiguous store.
6. Tail/alignment safety (mandatory, this is where past runs broke): the NCHW vector path requires `npix % 4 == 0` (else `c*npix + p0` is unaligned — 131×131 gives npix=17161). Templatize the kernel on `bool VEC`; host launches VEC=true only when `(npix & 3) == 0`, else VEC=false. Additionally, a partial pixel tile (`np = min(64, npix-p0) < 64`) must take the scalar path for the store phase.
7. VEC=false path: same 64×64 tiling and same smem, but scalar loads/stores with `p0+lane < npix` guards — a warp still covers 32 contiguous pixels per channel row, so coalescing is preserved and the awkward shape does not regress below its current 1.84x.
8. Zero-init nothing; every smem element written in the load phase is guarded by the same `np` bound used in the store phase, so no unwritten-tail read can occur — assert this by clamping both phases with the identical `np` variable.
9. Host side: unchanged signatures except adding the VEC template dispatch; keep `dim3 g(ceil(npix/64), B)`, block 256. Remove the now-dead `TP` constant and the `silu_f` dead helper.
10. Validate all 4 shapes (8×64×128, 2×64×64, 4×256×256, 1×131×131) against the reference at atol 0.0027; re-profile to confirm gn_apply2 DRAM% rises and duration falls, and confirm gn_apply1/gn_stats timings are byte-identical (untouched).

strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Batch-chunked multi-stream pipelining: GroupNorm statistics are per-(sample,group), so the whole block is exactly independent across batch elements. Split the batch into chunks and run the full conv1->stats->apply1->conv2->stats->apply2 chain for each chunk on its own CUDA stream, so an SM-bound conv of one chunk overlaps the DRAM-bound GN kernels (80% DRAM, <47% SM) of another. This hides most of the ~300 us GN time under the ~950 us conv time; bit-identical math (same per-sample reductions).
strategy.modification_plan:
CHECKLIST
1. Keep every existing kernel body byte-identical (gn_stats_p1/p2, gn_apply1, gn_apply2 already take npix/B via grid.y); the ONLY change is host-side scheduling in fused_block: replace the single monolithic sequence with a per-batch-chunk pipeline issued on N side streams.
2. Exact code action for the split: compute `int ns = (B>=4)?4:((B>=2)?B:1); int cb = (B+ns-1)/ns;` if `ns==1` execute the current code path verbatim (this preserves the 1x256x131x131 shape exactly). Otherwise loop `for (int s=0,b0=0; b0<B; ++s, b0+=cb) { int nb=min(cb,B-b0); ... }` and inside use `x.narrow(0,b0,nb)` / `out.narrow(0,b0,nb)` views only.

METHOD STEPS
3. Stream pool: `static thread_local std::vector<c10::cuda::CUDAStream> pool; if (pool.empty()) for(int i=0;i<4;++i) pool.push_back(c10::cuda::getStreamFromPool());` (created once, reused across the 12 timed forwards).
4. Hoist chunk-invariant work onto the main stream BEFORE the loop: `w1l = w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `w2l = w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `xc = x.contiguous()`, and the single output allocation `out = at::empty({B,256,H,W}, opts)`. Do NOT allocate y1/y1n/y2/scale/shift globally; allocate them inside the chunk body so the caching allocator binds them to the side stream.
5. Fork: `at::cuda::CUDAEvent fork; fork.record(at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()); for(auto& s : used_streams) fork.block(s);` so every side stream waits for the caller's prior work and for step-4 allocations/copies.
6. Chunk body: `{ c10::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(pool[s%4]); auto xb = xc.narrow(0,b0,nb); auto xl = xb.contiguous(ChannelsLast); auto y1 = at::conv2d(xl,w1l,{},1,1,1,1); gn_stats(y1,...,nb,npix,...); gn_apply1<<<dim3(gridx,nb),256,0,cur>>>(...); auto y2 = at::conv2d(y1n,w2l,{},1,1,1,1); gn_stats(y2,...,nb,npix,...); auto ob = out.narrow(0,b0,nb); gn_apply2<<<dim3(gridp,nb),256,0,cur>>>(y2,xb,...,ob,npix); }` — every kernel launch uses `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` (already the case inside gn_stats), which the guard redirects to the side stream. Grid.y becomes `nb` and all image base offsets are already computed from `blockIdx.y * npix * 256` on the narrowed pointers, so no kernel edit is needed (narrow on dim 0 keeps contiguity).
7. Allocator safety: after the narrow, call `out.record_stream(pool[s%4]);` and `xc.record_stream(...)` (only if xc is a freshly made contiguous copy) so blocks are not recycled before the side stream finishes.
8. Join: for each used stream `at::cuda::CUDAEvent ev; ev.record(stream); ev.block(main_stream);` before `return out;`. This makes the returned tensor safe on the caller's stream and keeps the harness's CUDA-event timing valid.
9. Issue order for maximum overlap: emit chunk 0's full pipeline first, then chunk 1, etc.; because each chunk's conv (SM-heavy, DRAM-light) is followed by GN (DRAM-heavy, SM-light), consecutive streams naturally interleave. Do not add any sync inside the loop.

GRID SIZING (must not deadlock): call `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&mb, gn_fused2, 256, 34816)` and `cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&nsm, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount,0)`; `maxBlocks = mb*nsm;` `bpb = max(1, min(maxBlocks/B, (npix+31)/32));` `chunk = (npix + bpb - 1)/bpb;` grid = dim3(B*bpb). Launch with `cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel((void*)gn_fused2, grid, dim3(256), args, 34816, stream)`; allocate `part` as `B*bpb*32*2` floats.
4. TAIL/AWKWARD-SHAPE SAFETY: chunk*bpb may exceed npix — clamp p1 and allow empty ranges (block still must reach `grid.sync()`; never `return` before the sync). Phase3 pixel loop must use the same clamped [p0,p1). Verify H*W=17161 (odd) shape writes every partial slot: zero-init `part` is unnecessary because phase2 reads exactly bpb entries all written in phase1.
5. FALLBACK: if `cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel` returns error or `maxBlocks < B`, keep the existing 3-kernel path (gn_stats_p1/p2/apply) unchanged — guarantees the large 4×256×256×256 shape never regresses.
6. LEAVE UNTOUCHED: both at::conv2d channels-last calls (vendor default-keep), the contiguous(ChannelsLast) calls, dtypes (fp32 storage, fp32 partials, double final reduce), and gn_apply2's residual/transpose math.
7. VALIDATE: all 4 shapes within atol (0.0027/0.0028/0.0030/0.0029); nsys launch count must drop 132→84 (11→7 per forward); confirm gn_stats_p2 no longer appears.

Same bytes, same dtype, fewer transactions.
